availableEvidence.description2: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. courseLedger.name: Native American Histories

availableEvidence.description2: This course introduces students to Native American history and life from the 19th through the 21st century.  It argues that power, fear, misogyny, education, genocide, and resilience shape the Indigenous past and present. We learn from the Native American scholars and 2Spirit youth that speak to and with the class. Exchange of cultural and intellectual knowledge also happens when we work with Lakota students to address contemporary challenges. Legislation, memoir, novels, and Indigenous children’s stories are central to our studies. So are the analyses of contemporary music and artistic expressions and exhibitions, as well as Hollywood and Indigenous film featuring Native American histories and lives.

Arts-based collaborations and a public-history project develop respectful, accessible accounts of historical and contemporary issues.
